dataset evidence: ID 1 (all visits) includes ID 2: respiratory visits are 22.2% of all visits; weekly r = 0.88. The KPI share for week t+2 is a function of the target.
potential consequence: A feature such as all visits or share in the target week would reproduce the target and inflate accuracy.
mitigation: Exclude every target-week quantity (all visits, share, age bands, spike flags). Use only weeks <= t. Asserted in §6.

risk: L2 Future information (hindsight panels, centred windows)
dataset evidence: C1's 581-facility common panel requires knowing 2024 presence; 9 facilities active 2020-2023 are excluded only because of 2024. Centred moving averages would also use t+1.
potential consequence: A model trained on survivors would look better than it would in real time (survivorship bias).
mitigation: No panel membership, annual totals or centred windows as features; only trailing windows ending at t.

dataset evidence: 2 identical extra rows (facility 08-105, 10 Jan 2023). Under a random split, a copy could fall in train and its twin in test.
potential consequence: Memorised rows score perfectly in test, with no generalisation.
mitigation: De-duplicate before any split (V3); assert unique (facility, origin week) keys and no key in two splits.

risk: L4 Repeated facilities and temporal autocorrelation
dataset evidence: Median lag-1 autocorrelation of facility weekly respiratory visits = 0.92. In a naive 80/20 random split of facility-weeks, 79% of test rows have the same facility's previous week in train; 665 facilities fall in both splits.
potential consequence: Test performance would measure interpolation between neighbouring weeks, not forecasting a future season.
mitigation: Chronological split by target week (§6). Facilities intentionally appear in all periods because the decision forecasts the same network; new facilities in test are counted.

risk: L5 Linked tables and slowly changing attributes
dataset evidence: 12,687 facility-dates have a type different from the facility's latest type (19 reclassified facilities). The only register available is dated 08-07-2022; 27 IDs are unmatched.
potential consequence: Back-filling the 2024 type, or a 2022 register, into 2020-2021 rows uses information not available then.
mitigation: Use the type recorded at week t. No register join; any future join must use a register vintage <= origin date.

risk: L6 Preprocessing learned on all data
status: Present in W1/C1, mitigated in W2
dataset evidence: V9 spike rule uses each facility's five-year median (45 flags); the median moves by 7.0 visits/day (median facility) when only 2020-2022 is used. W1's 30% alert line was chosen after viewing all years.
potential consequence: Scaling, imputation or thresholds tuned on test weeks leak their distribution into training.
mitigation: Spike flags are not model features. Imputer, scaler, encoder and alert threshold are fitted on training rows only (§6.5-6.6).

risk: L7 Data vintage and late revisions
dataset evidence: Archives were downloaded on 24 Sep 2026, long after the events. DEIS updates daily, but we have only one vintage, so we cannot measure how week t counts looked at the time.
potential consequence: Back-filled final counts are more complete than real-time counts; historical evaluation would be optimistic.
mitigation: Treat as a limitation; archive weekly snapshots before any operational use; add a reporting-lag scenario.

risk: L8 Test-period exposure in W1/C1 EDA
dataset evidence: C1 reported 2024 peak weeks (12-18 May 2024, 45.56%) and annual 2024 shares before this split existed.
potential consequence: Choices (e.g. calendar features, the May framing) may already be shaped by 2024.
mitigation: Declare the 2024 holdout as "previously explored"; freeze features before any test use; use it only once, as a robustness check.
